related_work.work_intent_goal: exercise canonical Environment persistence through the Control socket
related_work.campaign_objective: MNCS Environmental Capability Intelligence & Continuous Improvement Campaign

outcome.implementation_change: Environment now accepts an exact owner-authorized checkout when it differs from the entry-time repository selection, and first post-grant claims resolve from the durable owner grant. Control re-resolves its clean registered Environment source against the current local main revision on each operation.
outcome.analysis_limit: The live grant and claim succeeded after the configured Environment root was fast-forwarded to pushed main. That local synchronization is recorded as an operational recovery. The observation does not yet establish that all MCP contexts automatically follow main or that reported multi-week friction has ended.

improvement_relation.basis: The initial live scope request was rejected before publication despite an exact owner approval and writable intent. Regression tests independently reproduced and fixed default-checkout vetoes during grant validation and post-grant claim acquisition. A long-lived Control service test verifies source selection follows a newly advanced main revision. The authenticated live scope grant and claim then bound the requested main linked checkout; the claim was released while the durable scope grant remained.
not_measured: whether Control source re-resolution alone removes the need to synchronize the configured root in every live bridge
future resource overhead of repeated source validation
cross-session recurrence and durable long-term resolution
